comments.author: @sylviadeGraven
comments.text:
As a proud Surinamese person living in the Netherlands, I would first like to thank you for bringing attention to Suriname. However, in my opinion, you have not presented the country entirely accurately.
I base this view on the video footage, your explanation of it, and especially the title of the video: “How people live in Suriname.” In my opinion, that title is far too broad compared to what you actually showed in the footage and explained.

No, this is NOT how we live in Suriname.

You mainly showed very limited footage of the interior of the country. I also question the authenticity of some of the images, for example the impression that Suriname has such crystal clear blue water that you can easily see the bottom, as shown in your footage.

Furthermore, you talk about Christmas while clearly showing people wearing winter clothing and winter hats. In Suriname, we celebrate New Year’s Eve very enthusiastically, and certainly not just with a little sparkler and definitely not while wearing a winter hat.

What you mainly seem to portray is that we live only in huts and in very primitive conditions. That is simply not an accurate representation of Suriname. There are many beautiful homes and villas in Suriname. We also drive very luxurious cars; we do not get around only by canoe or by foot.

There are also many successful entrepreneurs in Suriname, particularly young entrepreneurs. They are certainly not all walking for kilometers carrying baskets on their heads.

You do show some footage of the city center, but you do not show the beautiful and luxurious homes or the types of cars that are commonly used in Suriname.

It is disappointing that foreigners so often portray Suriname in this way as if the country is always primitive and poor. Suriname is not only rich in culture; it also has many wealthy and successful people.

We are more than our colonial past. It is time to move beyond that narrative as well.

And finally, if you want to show the “huts” of Suriname, then at least show the full picture. These are also the “huts” in Suriname:
